newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom loses legal battle with regulator.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom loses legal battle with regulator.

text.p: The British High Court on Friday rejected a legal challenge brought by British Telecommunications Plc against tougher powers for industry regulator Oftel.

The court confirmed the legality of a new fair trading condition Oftel has introduced into BT's licence. The condition seeks to prohibit any abuse by a dominant operator and the making of restrictive, anti-competitive agreements.
BT had accepted the condition and a series of associated price controls but reserved the right to test the legality of the reinforced Oftel powers.

Oftel Director General Don Cruickshank welcomed the decision and said the condition would be introduced to the licences of 44 international telephone operators who were on Thursday granted full access to the British market.
They include U.S. giant AT&T and the Global One alliance between Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint of the U.S.

"With the granting yesterday of 44 international licences - ending the international facilities duopoly - the UK is now the most open telecommunications market in the world," Cruickshank said in a statement.

"Today's confirmation of the lawfulness of the Fair Trading Condition, which appears in those International Facilities Licences as well as BT's licence, means that the UK regulatory regime will be well equipped to deal with the dynamic competitive market of the future," he added.
BT said the right approach to introducing tighter controls on anti-competitive behaviour was through legislation and urged the government to give the matter urgent consideration.
